pairs.question: Quibus in terris gestum negotium est?
pairs.answer: Illo, illo, inquam, loco quem videtis.
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses and answers his own question in a catechism series. Question and answer are adjacent and complete; nothing cut. The next unit (Extra ordinemne...) begins a new question.

pairs.question: Extra ordinemne pecunia est data?
pairs.answer: Immo vero nummus nullus sine litteris multis commotus est.
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question (-ne) with self-answer. Stripped angle brackets from nu<l>lus keeping nullus. Answer ends at first full stop; what follows (Quae est igitur ista accusatio...) is a new rhetorical question.

pairs.question: A quibus versuras tantarum pecuniarum factas esse dicunt? a Gallis?
pairs.answer: A civibus Romanis qui negotiantur in Gallia.
pairs.derivation: Cicero asks (A quibus... a Gallis?), gives a dismissive non-answering interjection (Nihil minus), re-asks (A quibus igitur?), then answers. Per answer-window guidance the non-answering deflections are skipped and the operative answering sentence (A civibus Romanis...) is taken; the re-question A quibus igitur? was omitted as framing of the answering exchange. The setup hoc praetore oppressam esse aere alieno Galliam precedes.

pairs.question: Potest igitur testibus iudex non credere?
pairs.answer: Cupidis et iratis et coniuratis et ab religione remotis non solum potest sed etiam debet.
pairs.derivation: Authorial question answered immediately by Cicero himself. Both adjacent and complete; what follows (Etenim si, quia Galli dicunt...) elaborates.

pairs.question: Quem Pisonem?
pairs.answer: Cogis me dicere inimicum meum Frugi.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange: the viator asks which Piso (quod erant plures), and Gracchus answers. Dropped the speech tags (et viator quaereret framing the question; inquit framing the answer). Normalized capitalization and terminal punctuation. The setup is that Gracchus had Piso summoned and the attendant asked which one because there were several.
